key_insight: Update-matched references help unlearning stay resistant to relearning without unnecessarily suppressing a model’s ability to learn new tasks.
engineering_relevance: For deployable LLMs that will continue to be updated, UMU offers a practical way to preserve post-update plasticity while reducing recovery of deleted knowledge.
method: Apply the same simulated relearning update to both the defended model and an undefended reference initialized from the unlearned model.
Use new-task learning as the selection signal so the model is judged on preserved plasticity, not only low relearning.
Compare against pre-update and update-matched references to isolate selective resistance from general capability loss.
evidence_signal: On TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen, UMU improved relearning resistance and plasticity across three base unlearning methods, reducing harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while increasing new-task accuracy by 3.5 points.
watch_item: The approach adds evaluation and training complexity because the defense must simulate the downstream update and depends on how well that update matches real deployment behavior.
paper_title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
